name: Village Library
description: Volunteers help run the library in the old 1891 schoolhouse, built from the logs of the village brewery. Quiet, warm, and free.
greeting: The tiled stove ticks as it warms.
A new shelf of crime novels has arrived.

hello: The new crime novels are on the left.
Do you know this house is older than the railway bridge?
read: Good choice. That one has a twist.
self_study: There's tea if your head hurts.
work: Thank you, dear. The shelves look lovely.
Good work. Not a single book out of place.
The book club left biscuits. Take one.
Someone returned a book from 1987. No fine, it's a miracle.
You found the missing atlas! Behind the radiator.
olli: He means well. He just means it very loudly.
Shh! Olli, this is a library!
He set up our wifi. Nobody else knows the password. Not even me.

lines: The old tiled stove is warm. Aili says it has been lit every winter since 1923, "except during the war, and that was the Russians' fault".
You put your hands on the tiled stove. For a moment, all is well with the world.
A sign on the stove: DO NOT DRY MITTENS HERE. Six mittens are drying on it.

olli.name: Olli
lines: Have you heard of my app? It's a to-do list. But with dark mode.
I'm not addicted to coffee. I'm a coffee-based life form.
Have you tried turning your life off and on again?
The library wifi password is "kirjasto". I hacked it. By asking.

then.message: Another chapter... the words are starting to blur together.

else.message: You lose yourself in a good book.

then.message: You read for hours, but it's all things you already know.

else.message: You take careful notes. Your next lessons should go more smoothly.

actions.label: Ask Olli for computer help
actions.description: Olli sits at the library computer every day, "helping". He knows a lot. He will make sure you know he knows.

then.message: Olli again. He remembers everything you got wrong last time and lists it, in order. You learn a little. Your eye twitches.

do.message: Olli fixes your problem, then explains three problems you didn't have, then why you should switch to Linux.
Olli: "Have you tried turning it off and on again?" He laughs at his own joke for a full minute. You learn a lot, though.
Olli pitches his blockchain startup for an hour. In between, you actually learn something useful.
Olli sighs loudly every time you click something. You learn fast, just to make it stop.
